content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge is weighing a collision in which each side presses its own chain (the challenger's seed/loins chain against the defender's link C1, and the defender's chain back), which is exactly the chain-against-chain collision K-C governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side. // Whether a single verse, or the chain read together, states a link in so many words is never the deciding test, for or against.", "room": "'never the deciding test, for or against': reading one, 'does not name Joseph as the begetter' and 'rests on the woman-route inference' are legitimate footing critiques identifying missing links; reading two, they are statement-absence demerits, since footing was already conceded to both chains before each 'but', leaving only what the chains state in so many words as the operative ground.", "why": "Having conceded that both chains are footed, the judge grounds UNDERDETERMINED in what each chain fails to state in so many words (naming, inference) rather than in any comparison of footing, which is precisely the stating-verse test K-C retires for either side."}
